name: kiesel
why: A from-scratch ECMAScript engine written in Zig, a fascinating look at how JavaScript engines are built from the ground up.

brief.what_it_is: Kiesel is described as a JavaScript engine written in Zig, and the scout notes call it a from-scratch ECMAScript engine. The homepage at kiesel.dev loaded, but it returned only a page title ("Kiesel JavaScript Engine") and script tags with no readable text, so I could not confirm features, inputs, or outputs from it. The Homebrew entry installs an executable named kiesel. Presumably it takes JavaScript source and runs it, but I did not verify that.
brief.why_it_exists: The scout notes frame it as a from-scratch look at how JavaScript engines are built from the ground up. I found no author statement of purpose.
brief.install_notes: Only the Homebrew formula data was available: the formula is named kiesel, its description is "JavaScript engine written in Zig", and it installs one executable, kiesel. I found no README or docs with build steps, runtime requirements, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: A complete ECMAScript engine written from scratch in Zig, rather than a wrapper around V8 or JavaScriptCore. That makes it a readable case study in how the pieces of a JS engine fit together.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release dates or commit activity. I could not reach a repository README: a guessed GitHub URL (github.com/kiesel-js/kiesel) returned 404, and the homepage links to nothing I could read.
brief.caveats: The homepage is effectively empty to a non-JavaScript fetch, so the brief rests on the Homebrew description and scout notes, not on the project's own documentation. Conformance level, performance, and completeness are unverified. The guessed repository URL may simply be wrong, so the real source may still exist elsewhere.
quotes: A from-scratch ECMAScript engine written in Zig, a fascinating look at how JavaScript engines are built from the ground up.
